title: Adaptive TTL + microbatch shaping: throughput–fidelity sweep and regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: quantify latency vs. generation-quality tradeoffs for a combined adaptive KV-cache TTL and microbatch-shaping change, and produce an automated regression-detection policy for rollouts. Motivation: previous experiments show non-linear interactions between cache TTL, prefix reuse, and microbatch size across heterogeneous workloads. We need an empirical sweep that captures tail latency, throughput, and signal-to-noise on quality metrics so the rollout can be gated by measurable thresholds rather than heuristics.

Scope:
- Evaluate four TTL strategies: zero (no prefix reuse), fixed short (5s), fixed medium (30s), and adaptive (TTL tuned by recent prefix-hit ratio and request latency window).
- Evaluate microbatch shaping policies: static microbatch sizes (1, 2, 4, 8) and an adaptive shaper that increases microbatch for long-running low-latency-tolerance streams while preserving p95 SLO.
- Cross-sweep combinations of TTL x microbatch x scheduling policy to find Pareto frontiers per workload class.
- Measure quality impact on three canonical workloads: conversational (chit-chat + followups), summarization (long-document condense), and instruction-following (multi-step code/data transforms).

Metrics:
- Latency: p50, p95, p99, and token emit latency + end-to-end RPC latency. Report both median and tail.
- Throughput: requests/sec and tokens/sec under steady load (saturating and non-saturating regimes).
- Cost proxy: GPU utilization and tokens-per-GPU-second.
- Quality: automated eval harness scores per workload: ROUGE-L (summaries), exact-match/intent-score (instruction tasks), and a composite hallucination-rate signal measured by fact-check subroutine. Also measure soft-similarity (embedding cosine) against golden responses to detect subtle drift.
- Statistical tests: use bootstrap confidence intervals across prompt shards; flag configurations where quality delta relative to baseline is statistically significant (p < 0.05) and exceed absolute thresholds defined below.

Success criteria / gates for rollout:
- No config allowed to promote to canary unless: (a) p95 latency does not exceed baseline by > 12% AND absolute p95 <= 220ms for hosted small models, (b) quality composite score drop <= 1.5% and hallucination-rate increase <= 3 percentage-points, (c) cost proxy improves or stays within 5% of baseline.
- Canary to production promotion requires 72h stable telemetry and no quality alerts in the golden prompt set.

Experiment matrix and infra:
- Stimuli: replay of production trace (sampled multimodal traffic) with synthetic amplification for each workload class to reach both sub-saturating and saturating regimes.
- Matrix: TTL values [0, 5s, 30s, adaptive], microbatch sizes [1,2,4,8,adaptive], scheduling modes [fair, latency-first, throughput-first]. Total combinations ~60; run each with 3 seeds across 3 hardware shapes (A100-80GB, H100-80GB, cheaper T4-equivalent for edge sim).
- Baseline: current stable config (TTL=30s, microbatch=4, scheduling=latency-first).
- Harness and artifacts: use eval-runner v2.3 (GitHub: github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pulls/1823) and a private Confluence doc with golden prompts (confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Adaptive-TTL-Eval).

Monitoring & regression detection:
- Continuous golden prompt set runs in parallel to traffic lanes; produce per-build diffs.
- Regression alert conditions: composite-quality drop >= 1.5% OR hallucination delta >= 3 percentage-points OR p95 latency increase >= 12% (each evaluated with CI overlap). On alert, auto-fail canary and revert traffic weighting to baseline.
- Dashboard: new tile in Console runtime perf view: 'Adaptive TTL Sweep' showing Pareto points, and a heatmap of quality vs p95 for each workload.

Rollout plan & safety:
- Short canary: promote to 5% traffic for 24h with heavy golden set runs; if stable, extend to 25% for 48h. If any regression alert fires, rollback immediately and open postmortem.
- Blockers: integration of adaptive-shaper into serving runtime requires deterministic behavior under preemption (ENG-77420 follow-up). If not merged, scope reduces to simulated adaptive shaper in eval harness only.

Deliverables:
- Experiment results (CSV + visualizations), PR with runtime flags and default configs, Console dashboard tile, regression gating policy encoded in release automation, and a short runbook for on-call.

Notes: this ticket focuses on evaluation and automated gate creation; production rollout work will be split into a follow-up depending on chosen config and safety policy.
